source_analysis.skill: Compute the actual derivative of the supplied function, independently assess the displayed derivative claim, substitute the actual function and derivative into the differential equation, and decide whether equality holds identically on the common domain.
reasoning_steps: Compare the actual derivative to statementI.
Substitute actual f and derivative into the ODE.
Determine identity on the common domain and select exactly the true statements.
invariants: Statements II and III have the same truth value: a differentiable function is a solution exactly when its actual derivative satisfies the ODE identically on domain.
The derivative used for II must be calculated from f rather than copied from a false statement I.
I can be independently true/false of II/III, allowing truth tuples000,100,011,111.
Use identity on shared domain, not equality at a single point; logs require x>0, reciprocals x!=0.
This is verification, not solving ODEs, applying initial conditions, integration or advanced existence/uniqueness.
permitted_variations: Within EACH recognizable power/exponential/log/trig/reciprocal family, independently vary derivative claim correctness and ODE coefficient or form so satisfying versus nonsatisfying is not fixed by family.
Vary small nonzero coefficients, integer exponents, inner linear rates, and signs while preserving existing differentiation rules and workload.
Hold f fixed and change claimed derivative only: I must toggle while II/III stay fixed. Hold f and derivative claim fixed and change ODE so identity fails: II/III must toggle while I stays fixed.
Rescale a homogeneous power/exponential solution and its derivative by same nonzero factor: truth should remain; irrelevant item IDs/order should not affect grading.
